title: The Imitation of Christ
subtitle: The Classic William Benham Translation – with a Plain-Language Note on Every Chapter and a 30-Day Practice
author: Thomas à Kempis
pd_statement: The Imitation of Christ was written in Latin in the early fifteenth century and is traditionally attributed to Thomas à Kempis (c. 1380–1471). This edition follows the English translation by William Benham (1831–1910), as printed with an introductory note in the Harvard Classics (1909); both are in the public domain. Benham’s wording, his numbering of the paragraphs and his Scripture references are kept; obvious printing errors are corrected.

headline: Seek the inner life.
Follow Christ.
Find true peace.
paras: After the Bible, no Christian book has been read more widely. Written in a quiet Dutch monastery almost six hundred years ago, The Imitation of Christ still speaks with startling directness about humility, inner peace, temptation, friendship with Christ and the love that makes every burden light.

This beautifully designed annotated edition presents the complete four books in William Benham’s classic translation and adds what today’s reader needs: an introduction to Thomas à Kempis and his world, a plain-language note and a small practice for every chapter, and a guided 30-day practice.
